stemBlocks.value: Think first: Twenty divides neatly by five, so dividing both sides first is the cleanest opening move.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p054-q03 from workbook page 54.

contentBlocks.value: Result: 20, which matches the right-hand side

strategyBlocks.value: Divide both sides by 5, then subtract 6 to isolate x.

whyThisWorks.value: Dividing both sides by 5 is the inverse of the multiplication that produced 5(x + 6), so it removes the outer factor while preserving equality. What remains, x + 6 = 4, is undone by subtracting 6. The negative solution is entirely legitimate: it simply means x sits two units below zero, and substituting it back confirms the original equation holds.

commonErrors.misconception: Rejecting x = −2 on the grounds that it is negative.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Rejecting x = −2 on the grounds that it is negative.

commonErrors.misconception: Expanding as 5x + 6 = 20 by not multiplying the 6.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Expanding as 5x + 6 = 20 by not multiplying the 6.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding 6 rather than subtracting it after dividing.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding 6 rather than subtracting it after dividing.

examTip.value: Always substitute your answer back into the original equation, not into a line of your own working. That way an earlier slip cannot hide behind a later one.
